title: Interaction modules — parking lot & proto PRD
body:
High-level idea:
A lightweight layer on top of generation that lets apps assemble, version, and reuse small 'interaction modules' (snippets + constraints + metadata) at runtime so responses are composable, cacheable, and auditable. Think of modules as first-class units (like components) you can call into the model pipeline instead of baking everything into one monolithic prompt.

Why this helps (hypotheses):
- Saves tokens by reusing stable pieces (legal disclaimers, product facts, templated examples).
- Makes A/B and rollouts easier (swap modules instead of full prompts).
- Enables fine-grained quality monitoring (module-level evals).
- Developer ergonomics: create library of team-approved modules.
- Better caching: store KV/prefixes per module to warm decoder faster.

Core concepts / vocabulary:
- Module: small unit (text template + optional instructions + schema) with id + version.
- Bundle: ordered list of modules + wiring (where outputs from module A feed into B).
- Invocation: API call to run bundle for a session or one-off request.
- Module runtime: deployable artifact that can be local (edge) or hosted, optionally quantized variant.

Rough user stories:
1) Developer: "As a product dev, I want to assemble a response bundle of modules (greeting, product-facts, call-to-action) so I can ship without rewriting prompts per feature."
2) Platform: "As an SRE, I want module-level cache keys so we can measure hit rates and evict stale fragments."
3) Legal/Policies: "As a compliance reviewer, I want to pin a vetted 'safety-statement' module to all bundles for a customer."
4) Product manager: "As a PM, I want to run a canary by swapping a single module to a new version for 10% traffic."

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create module API: create/update/list/get module metadata + version.
- Compose bundle API: create a bundle referencing module ids + default ordering.
- Runtime: execute bundle with simple wiring; return combined text + per-module token counts and latency.
- Dashboard: per-module metrics (invocations, p50/p95 latency, avg tokens, cache hit rate).
- Rollout primitives: bundle-level and module-level traffic split (0/10/50/100).

API sketches (proto):
- POST /modules {name, template, constraints, visibility, tags} -> module_id
- POST /bundles {name, module_ids: [id:v], wiring: [{from,to}], defaults} -> bundle_id
- POST /invoke {bundle_id, session_id, input_slots: {...}, overrides: {module_id:partial}} -> {combined_text, module_traces}
Notes: keep payloads tiny, return token accounting per module for billing.

Monitoring / telemetry:
- Per-module: calls, errors, redactions, avg tokens returned, p50/p95 latency
- Per-bundle: composition latency, error surface (which module failed)
- Cost telemetry: tokens saved vs equivalent monolithic prompt (estimate)
- Quality hooks: tie evals to module versions (run unit prompts)

Architectural thoughts (lightweight):
- Store modules in metadata service (small DB row per module + versioned template).
- At runtime, expand templates into a single prompt but annotate span boundaries for KV caching and token accounting.
- Cache keys: bundle_id + module_version_hash + prefix_signals (user locale, product_id).
- Optional: compile-hot bundles into optimized runtime form (pre-tokenized, pinned KV warm state) for high-throughput customers.

UX / Console ideas:
- Module library browser: filter by tags, owner, last-modified, preview rendered output for sample inputs.
- Bundle composer: drag-drop modules, add wiring, test-run with sample session.
- Module approval workflow: draft -> reviewed -> approved -> pinned.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (spike): implement simple module metadata + expand-on-invoke in a dev sandbox (2 sprints).
- Phase 1 (MVP): public API + dashboard + basic rollout controls (3 sprints).
- Phase 2: caching, compiled bundles, autoscaling optimizations, private deploy integration (4 sprints).

Metrics for success:
- Developer adoption: 20 internal teams using modules in 3 months (internal trial).
- Token savings: measurable >=10% token reduction for templated-response flows within 6 weeks of adoption.
- Latency: p95 bundle execution within target SLO (depends on model) — must not regress on critical paths.
- Quality: no increase in downstream complaint rate (Safety/CS) after module rollout.

Open questions / risks:
- Granularity: how small is too small? (too many modules could add orchestration overhead).
- Security: modules with secrets or customer PII — how to enforce redaction/pinning and access control?
- Billing model: charge by bundle invocations vs tokens; need to align with existing per-token billing.
- Cache correctness: stale module versions vs pinned deployments — need explicit invalidation paths.
- Model hallucinations when stitching modules: how to ensure coherence across module boundaries?

Quick experiments to validate:
- Take 3 existing flows (support reply, onboarding copy, billing FAQ) and refactor into modules; measure token delta, latency, and dev time to change text. (Spike: 1 week)
- Implement per-module token accounting in a prod-like sandbox and surface in console. (Spike: 1 week)

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Create spike tickets: RED-4821 (spike module runtime), RED-4822 (console composer mock), RED-4823 (telemetry plumbing).
- [ ] Sync with Mira on approval workflow constraints (legal bounds).
- [ ] Quick design sketch for module UX — hand off to design.
- [ ] Run 2 internal demos with Solutions Eng + Support to collect edge cases.

Notes to self:
- Keep MVP small: metadata + expand-on-invoke + per-module telemetry. Avoid building full compile/quantize path initially.
- Consider integration points with Dedicated/Private early — modules are especially valuable for enterprise pinning.

References / inspiration:
- Similar to componentized email templates but for model output.
- Think about offering a marketplace of verified modules for common domains.

Parking-lot ideas (non-MVP):
- Module-level fine-tuning or instruction-tuning bundles (train small adapter per module).
- Cross-tenant module marketplace with ACLs and revocation.
- Offline compilation into edge-friendly artifacts for on-prem.

Tagged tickets / people:
- RED-4821 (spike) -> assigned: @noah.garcia
- UX mock -> assigned: @mira.shah
- Legal review -> ticket CONF-7153 (link above)

End of pad. Random fragments I scribbled:
- "module pins" should be immutable at v1; updates create v2 to keep traceability.
- Put module hashes into request logs for quick cross-reference.
- Explore storing module rendered tokens separately to speed prefix caching.
